OBJECTIVE
Produce the written audit of the CURRENT mobile mode of the codx-junior web client (Vue 3 + Vuex + vue-router + daisyUI/Tailwind + dockview). OUTPUT FILE
docs/mobile/mobile-current-status.md (create folder if missing). Single markdown document, Spanish/English as used in repo comments (English preferred). Keep it stable in structure so later updates can be diffed.

1. Executive summary (max 10 lines): what breaks on a phone today, business impact, and the 3 root causes.
2. Module & route inventory table: for EVERY app/module list — appKey, visible title, route name + path, resolved component, desktop mode (panel?) vs single mode (route?), and mobile status (OK / degrades / broken / unknown).    - src/config/apps.js (APPS registry — single source of truth for "how to open an app")
   - src/router/index.ts (project-scoped routes, /:projectName/...)
   - src/config/appComponentsMap.js (appKey -> lazy component)

   D3 No mobile chrome at all: App.vue renders <RouterView/> with no app bar, no title, no back button, no bottom navigation; each screen invents its own.
   D4 Mode comes from the route, not the device: opening .../desktop on a phone mounts the dockview workspace.
   D5 Rich payloads travel in memory (setPendingParams): refresh / back-forward / shared link loses chat, team, channel, workspace, member → screens receive undefined.

   D9 No shared mobile primitives: no page header/back component, no bottom nav, no safe-area-inset handling, no scroll-lock, body{overflow:hidden} + h-full assumptions in index.html, inconsistent touch-target sizes.
7. Duplication map: components that exist twice for mobile/desktop or that duplicate content blocks (GlobalSettings desktop aside vs mobile drawer with 10 duplicated v-if branches, ChatEntry vs ChatEntryMobile, default.vue/built-in toolbars of each screen).
8. Constraints & risks for the refactor (dockview is desktop-only, deep links must keep working, per-project URL prefix, saved layouts in localStorage, eruda debug hook in main.ts).
9. Annex: proposed target principles (one navigation model, one page chrome component, one viewport source of truth) — 1 page max, no code.

RULES
- Read the files; do not trust this description blindly. Report any finding that no longer reproduces as "already fixed".
- No code changes. Documentation only. Cite file paths (and line numbers when useful) for every claim.
- Markdown tables, no screenshots required.

ACCEPTANCE
- docs/mobile/mobile-current-status.md exists, follows the 9 sections, every app from config/apps.js appears in the inventory, and each defect has file evidence + severity.
- Summary reply to the task lists: file path, number of modules inventoried, number of defects by severity, and the 3 root causes.

request.description:
OBJECTIVE
Build a functional, clickable HTML mockup of mobile strategy A for the codx-junior web client, so management can compare the three approaches side by side in a 5-minute walkthrough.

An app-like mobile shell that every module inherits:
- Fixed top app bar: back arrow (or hamburger on root screens), screen title, one contextual action, project switcher on the right.
- Fixed bottom tab bar with 4 destinations: Home (management dashboard), Tasks (kanban), Chat, More.
- "More" opens a bottom sheet with the remaining destinations grouped: Work (Wiki, Docs, Knowledge, Activity, Git), Settings (Project settings, Global settings, Account), Infra, Analytics, Vibe Coding.

- Safe-area padding (env(safe-area-inset-*)) and 44 px minimum touch targets.

1. Home / management dashboard — with the new top bar + bottom tab bar, tab "Home" active.
2. Tasks — board list, then one board opened (column tabs horizontally scrollable), bottom tab "Tasks" active, back arrow visible.
3. Chat — chat list, then one conversation with fixed composer above the tab bar.
4. More — bottom sheet open (dimmed backdrop), showing the grouped destinations.
5. Any screen with the project switcher open (small overlay), to show where multi-project lives.
Interactions must work with mock data in memory: tab switching, back navigation between stacked screens, bottom sheet open/close, project switch changing the project name in the top bar. No backend, no build step: one self-contained .html file (public CDN libs allowed).

docs/mobile/strategy-A-app-shell.html (self-contained) and docs/mobile/strategy-A-notes.md (max 1 page: navigation rules, which existing components can be reused — App.vue, DesktopSidebar.vue, config/apps.js registry — what must be created, effort estimate in days as optimistic/likely/pessimistic, and the top 3 risks).

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
- Visual language must match the current app: daisyUI 5 / Tailwind dark theme (base-100/200/300, primary, secondary, accent), FontAwesome icons, dense but readable.

request.description:
OBJECTIVE
Write the audit of the CURRENT mobile mode of the codx-junior web client (Vue 3 + Vuex + vue-router 5 + daisyUI 5/Tailwind 4 + dockview-vue). It is the baseline document of the "Mobile Refactor" board.

OUTPUT FILE
docs/mobile/mobile-current-status.md (create the folder if missing). Stable section structure so later updates can be diffed.

REQUIRED SECTIONS
1. Executive summary (max 10 lines): what breaks on a phone today, the user impact, the 3 root causes.
2. Module & route inventory table for EVERY app: appKey, title, route name + path, resolved component, desktop mode (dockview panel?) vs single mode (route?), mobile status (OK / degrades / broken / unknown). Build it from src/config/apps.js, src/router/index.ts and src/config/appComponentsMap.js, and flag every mismatch between the three (app key without a registered route, route whose component is missing, key only in the component map...).
3. Navigation model today: mode derived from the route (isDesktopMode() === route name 'codx-junior-split'), config/apps.js registry + router/navigate.js openApp(), AppRouteView.vue resolution (meta.app), and the in-memory payload hand-off setPendingParams/getPendingParams.
4. Shell audit: src/App.vue, src/components/desktop/DesktopSidebar.vue, src/components/desktop/Desktop.vue, src/main.ts, index.html.
5. Per-screen consistency audit for the 10 heaviest screens (ChatView/Chat, KanbanBoardView, GlobalSettings, ProjectSettings, KnowledgeView, VibeCodingView, TeamView, InfraView, FileExplorerPanel, ManagementDashboardView): own header? own sidebar/drawer? own scroll container? works at 375 px? has a way back?
6. Defect list with file evidence, severity (blocker/high/medium/low) and one-line fix direction. Verify each of these before writing it:
   D1 Two conflicting definitions of "mobile": src/store/ui.js handleResize (width <= 1024) vs src/App.vue (window.innerWidth < 768) vs src/components/chat/ProfileDrawer.vue (< 1024). Describe what happens in the 768-1024 band.
   D2 No visible global navigation on mobile: App.vue collapses the sidebar on every route change and the only expand controls live inside the off-canvas panel (translateX(-100%)).

# Mobile mode — current status audit

> Status document for the **Mobile Refactor** board.
> Scope: the customer-facing web client (`/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/client`).
> Method: static reading of the router, the app registry, the shell and the heaviest screens.
> **No device testing was performed for this version** — every "mobile status" below is inferred from the code
> structure. Items marked 🟥 are confirmed by code; items marked 🟨 need a device check.

---

## 1. Executive summary

On a phone the application **cannot be navigated**. The shell renders only the current screen with no app bar,
no title, no back button and no bottom navigation; the one navigation surface (the sidebar) is an off-canvas
panel that is collapsed on every route change and whose only open controls live *inside* the closed panel.
On top of that the "is this a phone?" question has three different answers in three files, the app decides
"desktop workspace vs single screen" from the **URL** instead of the device, and every screen invents its own
header, sidebar and scroll container — so the same product looks like 40 different products.

**Three root causes**

1. **No mobile shell.** There is no persistent navigation/chrome owned by the application; each screen is
   responsible for its own navigation and most simply have none.
2. **No single source of truth for viewport / mode.** Three breakpoints (`768`, `1024`, and a route name) decide
   what "mobile" means, in three different places.
3. **Two parallel UI stacks.** Desktop renders dockview panels; mobile renders routes through
   `AppRouteView`. Some modules resolve to a *different component* in each path (chat, workspaces, browsers, home),
   which is why behaviour and layout diverge between the modes.

**Business impact:** the product is effectively desktop-only. Phones and small tablets are a first-class
support surface for chat/task triage, and today they cannot even reach the screens.

---

## 2. Module & route inventory

Sources of truth (and they disagree — see §2.1):

- `src/config/apps.js` → `APPS`: the registry that decides *how an app is opened*.
- `src/router/index.ts` → project-scoped routes, all under `/:projectName/...`.
- `src/config/appComponentsMap.js` → `appKey → component` (lazy `defineAsyncComponent`).

| # | appKey | Title | Route (name → path) | Component (route) | Component (panel) | Desktop = panel | New phone route | Mobile status |

| 26 | `log-viewer` | Logs | `log-viewer` → `/:projectName/logs` | `LogViewer` | `LogViewer` | yes | yes | 🟨 unknown |
| 27 | `chat-logs` | Chat logs | `chat-logs` → `/:projectName/chat-logs` | `LogsAnalyzerDashboard` | `LogsAnalyzerDashboard` | yes | yes | 🟥 degrades |
| 28 | `decision-model-logs` | Decision model logs | `decision-model-logs` → `/:projectName/decision-model-logs` | `DecisionModelLogs` | `DecisionModelLogs` | yes | yes | 🟨 unknown |
| 29 | `metrics` | Metrics | `metrics` → `/:projectName/metrics` | `MetricsViewer` | `MetricsViewer` | yes | yes | 🟨 unknown |
| 30 | `analytics` | Analytics | `analytics` → `/:projectName/analytics` | `MetricsDashboard` | `MetricsDashboard` | yes | yes | 🟨 unknown |
| 31 | `api-monitoring` | API monitoring | `api-monitoring` → `/:projectName/api-monitoring` | `ApiMonitoringView` | `ApiMonitoringView` | yes | yes | 🟨 unknown |
| 32 | `team-channel` | Channel | `team-channel` → `/:projectName/team-channel/:channelId` | `TeamChannel` | `TeamChannel` | yes | yes | 🟨 needs payload (§6 D5) |
| 33 | `team-dm` | Direct message | `team-dm` → `/:projectName/team-dm/:dmId` | `TeamDM` | `TeamDM` | yes | yes | 🟨 needs payload (§6 D5) |
| 34 | `team-media-library` | Media Library | `team-media-library` → `/:projectName/team-media-library/:teamId` | `TeamMediaLibrary` | `TeamMediaLibrary` | yes | yes | 🟨 needs payload (§6 D5) |
| 35 | `vibe-coding` | Vibe Coding | `vibe-coding` → `/:projectName/vibe-coding` | `VibeCodingView` | `VibeCodingView` | yes | yes | 🟥 degrades (multi-panel splitter) |

**Routes with no registry entry:** `root` (bootstrap), `home`, `chats` (chat list, `QuickChatView`),
`browser-session`, `codx-junior-split` (`/:projectName/desktop/*` → `Desktop` = dockview workspace), catch-all redirect.

**Registry/component entries not reachable as a route:** `window`, `app-window` (fallback component), `tabComponent`,
`ViewProperties`, `EmptyStateWelcome`.

### 2.1 Registry vs router divergences (all confirmed by reading both files)

| Divergence | Effect |
|---|---|
| `APPS.home.component = 'home'` (`CodxWelcomeView`) but route `home` sets `meta.app = 'management-dashboard'` | "Home" is a different screen depending on the entry point |
| `APPS.chat.component = 'chat'` (`views/ChatView.vue`) but route `chat` mounts `QuickChatView.vue` | desktop panel and phone screen are **two different chat UIs** |
| `APPS.workspaces.component = 'workspaces'` (`WorkspacesManager`) but route `workspaces` mounts `WorkspaceView` | same |
| `APPS['browser-sessions'].component = 'browser-sessions'` (`BrowserSessionList`) but route `browsers` mounts `BrowsersSessionManager` | same |
| `router/navigate.js → browsers.open()` creates a panel with `component: 'browser-viewer'` | `browser-viewer` exists in neither `APPS` nor `appComponentsMap` → silent dead panel |
| `views/DesktopSidebar.vue` reads `$storex.$router.$navigation.getWorkspaceId()` / `.isDesktopMode` | works only because `router/index.ts` attaches `$navigation`; a second, older navigation object (`router.$navigate`) was removed and any leftover reference is dead code |

---

## 3. Navigation model as it exists today

```
URL  /:projectName/<segment>
        │
        ├── segment === "desktop"  → route name "codx-junior-split" → Desktop.vue → dockview panels
        │                                                            (many apps side by side)
        └── any other segment      → "single mode" → AppRouteView.vue
                                          │  reads route.meta.app
                                          ├── APPS[appKey]            (src/config/apps.js)
                                          ├── APP_COMPONENTS_MAP[...] (lazy component)
                                          └── params: getPendingParams() || route.params + query
```

- **Mode is derived from the route, not from the device** — `isDesktopMode()` in `src/router/navigate.js` is
  literally `$router.currentRoute.value.name === 'codx-junior-split'`.
- **`openApp(appKey, payload)`** is the unified opener: single mode → `router.push(def.route(payload))`;
  desktop mode → `$storex.ui.showApp({...})` which creates a dockview panel.
- **Payload hand-off**: objects that cannot live in a URL (chat, team, channel, member, workspace) are stashed in
  the in-memory map `PENDING` (`setPendingParams`) and read back by `AppRouteView`. There is no persistence.
- **Bootstrap**: `/` → guard redirects to `/:projectName` (`home`), whose `meta.app` is `management-dashboard`.
  So the phone landing screen is the cross-project management dashboard.

Consequences:

- A phone that receives `.../desktop` (bookmark, history, "open in new window") gets the dockview workspace.
- A phone that reloads a screen with a pending payload gets an app with `params = { …route.params }`, i.e. usually
  `undefined` for `chat`/`team`/`channel`.
- Nothing in the URL tells the user where they are: no re-usable title, no back stack semantics.

---

## 4. Shell audit

### `src/App.vue` (the mobile shell that does not exist)

- Root layout: `<Login>` or `<div class="flex">` containing `DesktopSidebar` (desktop rails **and** the mobile
  overlay, both from the same component) + `grow` wrapper + `<RouterView/>` + `<Toast>` + the global "New project"
  modal.
- `isMobile` is computed **locally**: `window.innerWidth < 768`, updated by a `resize` listener.
- On `created()` the mobile sidebar is collapsed, and it is collapsed again on **every** `$route` change.
- There is **no app bar, no title, no back button, no bottom navigation, no safe-area padding**.
- `isFullScreenRoute` only covers `route.name === 'solopreneur'`.

### `src/components/desktop/DesktopSidebar.vue` (~450 lines, two products in one file)

- `v-if="isMobile"` branch: fixed overlay + `aside` with `transform: translateX(-100%)` when
  `$storex.ui.sidebarCollapsed`, plus the overlay backdrop.
- `v-else` branch: the desktop icon-rail / expanded sidebar with width animation, wallet, daily spend, footer menu.
- Both branches duplicate the header, the `AppsSection`/`WorkspacesSection` block and the footer menu.
- Expand controls (`toggleCollapse`, and the collapsed-rail button) exist **only inside the panel**. On mobile the
  panel starts off-screen, so once collapsed there is no visible way to open it (see D2).

### `src/components/desktop/Desktop.vue`

- Hosts `<dockview-vue>` and registers every component from `ALL_COMPONENTS`.
- Syncs panels with `$storex.ui.openApps` (`syncPanelsWithApps`), persists layout to `localStorage`
  (`projectLayout_<project>`), restores it on project change, shows an error toast for failed panels.
- Drag/split/tab UI is designed for pointer + large screens; nothing suppresses it on small viewports.

### `src/main.ts` / `index.html`

- Global mixin injects `$storex`, `$ui`, `$projects`, `$app`, `$project`, `$session`, `$user`, `$users`, `$chats`,
  `$teams`, `$media`, `$globalSettings`, `$service` into **every** component.
- Mobile debugging hook: `eruda` is loaded from a CDN when `navigator.userAgent` matches `Mobi|Android`.
- `index.html` sets `body{ overflow: hidden; height:100% }` and `#app{ height:100% }` — the standard
  `100vh` + virtual-keyboard problem, with no viewport-unit or `visualViewport` handling anywhere.

---

## 5. Per-screen consistency audit

| Screen | Own header? | Own sidebar/drawer? | Own scroll container? | Works at 375 px? | Way back? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `views/ChatView.vue` (+ `Chat`, `ChatSidebar`, `ChatPanelHeader`) | yes (chat header) | yes (`ChatSidebar`, collapsible "compact") | yes, multiple nested | 🟥 no (fixed sidebars, monaco, 400 px editor heights) | only via the sidebar |
| `components/kanban/board/KanbanBoardView.vue` | yes (board toolbar, filters, view switcher) | no | yes | 🟥 no (columns are side-by-side) | a `fa-circle-arrow-left` that resets the board, not the route |
| `views/GlobalSettings.vue` | yes, **twice** (desktop `<aside>` + mobile drawer) | daisyUI `drawer` hand-rolled | yes, twice | 🟨 partially (10 duplicated `v-if` content blocks) | drawer overlay only |
| `views/ProjectSettings.vue` | own tabs | — | yes | 🟨 | no |
| `views/KnowledgeView.vue` | yes (title + tabs) | no | yes | 🟨 search usable, results dense | no |
| `views/VibeCodingView.vue` (+ `VibeCodingHeader`) | yes (2-row toolbar) | no | yes | 🟥 no (vertical splitter + 3 panels) | no |
| `views/TeamView.vue` (+ `TeamBar`, `TeamQuickBar`) | yes | yes (`TeamBar`, collapsible) | yes | 🟨 | no |
| `views/infra/InfraView.vue` | yes | rail + drawers | yes | 🟨 tables overflow | no |
| `components/filebrowser/FileExplorerPanel.vue` | no | fixed `w-64` tree | yes | 🟥 no (tree takes 256 px of 375) | no |
| `views/ManagementDashboardView.vue` | yes | left rail of sections | yes | 🟨 rail + content compete for width | no (it is the root) |

**Pattern:** every screen answers the same four questions (header, navigation entry, scroll, back) differently,
and six of ten answer "no" to back.

---

## 6. Defect list

| ID | Severity | Defect | Evidence | Fix direction |

# Mockups brief — mobile strategy, 3 approaches

> Audience: **Mockups / Designer** profile (owner of this brief), reviewed by the
> **Mobile Refactor** board owner.
> Input documents: `docs/mobile/mobile-current-status.md` (v1 audit) and
> `docs/mobile/status-verification-delta.md` (v2 corrections — **read this first**).
> Deliverable of this brief: three *different* mobile strategies, mocked at the same
> fidelity so they can be compared and one can be chosen.

---

## 1. What must be designed

The product is a project-scoped workspace with **35 registered apps**
(`src/config/apps.js`) rendered either as dockview panels (desktop) or as one route at a
time (`AppRouteView`). On a phone today there is **no chrome at all**: `<RouterView/>`
fills the screen, the navigation drawer exists but has **no visible trigger**, and each
screen invents its own header, sidebar and scroll container.

The brief is **not** "make these screens responsive one by one". It is:

> Give the product **one** mobile navigation model, **one** page shell and **one**
> decision about who owns navigation (the shell) versus content (the screen) — then show
> three *structurally different* ways to get there.

## 2. Hard constraints (apply to all three approaches)

| # | Constraint |
|---|---|
| C1 | Phones must **never** mount the dockview workspace (`.../desktop`), even if the URL says so |
| C2 | Deep links keep working: every route is `/:projectName/...`; identity (chat id, board, file path) must be recoverable from the URL |
| C3 | Touch targets ≥ 44×44 px; no hover-only affordance; nothing important in the top-right corner |
| C4 | Safe areas: `env(safe-area-inset-top)` under the status bar, `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` under the home indicator |
| C5 | Sticky app bar ≈ 56 px, bottom navigation ≤ 5 destinations (last may be "More") |
| C6 | The virtual keyboard must not cover the chat composer or a form's primary action |
| C7 | Long content is horizontally scrollable (code blocks, tables, kanban columns) — never clipped |
| C8 | Dark theme tokens only (daisyUI `base-*` / `primary` / `secondary`), icons = Font Awesome as used today |
| C9 | Every destination reachable from the bottom bar/More in **≤ 2 taps** from anywhere |
| C10 | The desktop experience must not regress: approaches must be shippable behind a flag |

## 3. Frames required for EACH approach

Primary canvas: **390 × 844** (iPhone 14 class). One tablet variant per approach: **768 × 1024**.

| # | Frame | What it must answer |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Landing / Home | Which screen does a phone land on, and what is the first navigation affordance? |
| F2 | Navigation surface | Bottom bar, drawer, launcher grid, or hybrid — open **and** closed states |
| F3 | A module with a list | Task Manager board (or planning list) — how does a dense board survive 390 px? |
| F4 | Chat | Conversation + composer + the moment the keyboard is open |
| F5 | A nested screen | File explorer / file viewer — journey *list → detail → back* |
| F6 | Settings | A screen that today ships **two** duplicated markup branches (`GlobalSettings.vue`) |
| F7 | State matrix | Loading, empty, error, offline for F3 and F4 as small tiles |
| F8 | Navigation diagram | The navigation graph + back-stack rules (what "back" means) |

Every frame must be annotated with: **where the back action lives**, **what `$ui.isMobile`
branch was deleted**, and **the route(s) it maps to**.

## 4. Comparison criteria (fill in for each approach)

| Criterion | Weight | How to judge |
|---|---|---|
| Learnability (find anything in ≤ 2 taps) | high | F9 walkthrough: open chat from Home, open a board, come back |
| Consistency across the 35 apps | high | does every screen get the same header/back/scroll, without per-screen work? |
| One-hand reachability | medium | primary actions inside the bottom 40% of the screen |
| Screens that cannot adapt (kanban, file explorer, vibe coding, infra tables) | high | does the approach have an answer other than "horizontal scroll"? |
| Implementation cost / risk | high | files touched, screens rewritten, desktop risk |
| Reversibility | medium | flag-gated? deletable? |
| Residual duplication removed | medium | §7 duplication map in the v1 audit |

## 5. Deliverables

1. `docs/mobile/approaches/01-*.md`, `02-*.md`, `03-*.md` — one document per approach,
   same structure: idea, navigation model, page shell, what changes (files), D-refs fixed,
   D-refs left, effort/risk, rollout flag, acceptance criteria, wireframes.
2. The frames above, exported as PNG/SVG in `docs/mobile/approaches/assets/<n>/`
   (or as inline HTML/SVG inside the approach document if binary export is not available).
3. A one-page comparison table appended to `docs/mobile/README.md` with a recommendation.

## 6. Non-goals

- No visual redesign of the desktop workspace (dockview, panels, splitters).
- No new product features, no new endpoints.
- No pixel-perfect brand work: this is a **navigation and shell** decision.

## 7. Open questions the mockups must resolve (not dodge)

1. **Bottom bar or drawer, or both?** A drawer-only model failed in production because the
   trigger is invisible; a bottom bar has only 5 slots for 35 apps.
2. **What does "back" mean** when screens are routes: browser history, an app-defined
   parent (`meta.parent`), or a per-module stack?
3. **Where does the project switcher live** on a phone (today it only exists inside the
   off-canvas drawer and inside `AppsSection`)?
4. **Do chat / workspaces / browsers keep two components** (desktop ↔ mobile) or become one
   adaptive component? This is the single biggest cost driver.

# Approach A — Shell-first ("wrap and ship")

> Status: proposed · Part of the **Mobile Refactor** board (design decision pending).
> Owner of the design: Mockups / Designer · Reviewer: board owner.
> Fixes the navigation *hole* with the smallest possible surface change.

---

## 1. Idea

Keep every existing screen exactly as it is. Add **one** wrapper between `App.vue` and
`<RouterView/>` that owns all the chrome a phone needs — app bar, back, bottom navigation,
safe areas, scroll container — and let each screen keep its own layout inside it.

The phone stops being "a desktop route rendered alone" and becomes "a desktop screen inside
a mobile shell". No screen is rewritten; the worst screens (kanban, file explorer, vibe
coding, infra) are accepted as degraded for now and addressed in later increments.

```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ ☰  Task Manager      ⌄  ⋯   │ ← MobileAppBar (56px, sticky, safe-area-top)
├─────────────────────────────┤
│                             │
│      current <RouterView/>  │ ← unchanged screen
│                             │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ ⌂     ✓     💬     📁    ⋯  │ ← MobileBottomBar (safe-area-bottom)
│Home  Tasks  Chat  Files More│
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

## 2. Navigation model

- **Bottom bar = the only global navigation.** 5 slots: Home, Tasks, Chat, Files, More.
  "More" opens a full-screen sheet that renders the whole registry (`APPS`) grouped by the
  same sections the desktop sidebar uses (`AppsSection` / `WorkspacesSection`).
- **App bar = context.** Title from `route.meta.title`, back arrow when `route.meta.parent`
  is set, right slot for one screen action.
- **Back** = `router.back()` when there is in-app history, otherwise `router.push(meta.parent)`
  (never leaves the app on a dead history entry).
- **Drawer stays**, but only as the *More* content on tablets (≥ 768 px); on phones the
  drawer is not used at all (it is the thing that failed).
- **Project switcher** moves into the app bar (it is the one global object on every screen).

## 3. Page shell contract

```
MobileShell
  ├── <MobileAppBar :title :back :actions/>
  ├── <main class="flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto">  ← the ONLY scroll container
  │      <RouterView/>
  └── <MobileBottomBar/>
```

Everything is driven by route meta, so a screen opts in with 3 lines:

```ts
{ path: '/:projectName/kanban/:board?/:boardName?', name: 'kanban',
  meta: { app: 'tasks', title: 'Task Manager', parent: 'home', primary: 'tasks' } }
```

## 4. What changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/components/mobile/MobileShell.vue` | **new** — grid layout + safe areas + scroll owner |
| `src/components/mobile/MobileAppBar.vue` | **new** — title / back / action slot |
| `src/components/layout/MobileBottomBar.vue` | **extend** — 5 slots, `primary` from route meta, real "New chat" action, registered `safe-area-bottom` utility |
| `src/composables/useViewport.js` | **new** — `phone` / `tablet` / `desktop` from one breakpoint table |
| `src/App.vue` | render `MobileShell` instead of the raw `<RouterView/>`; delete the local `isMobile`; delete the duplicate backdrop; **keep** `DesktopSidebar` for `desktop` only |
| `src/store/ui.js` | `handleResize` delegates to `useViewport`; expose `viewport` (`phone`/`tablet`/`desktop`) next to the legacy `isMobile` |
| `src/router/index.ts` | add `meta.title` / `meta.parent` / `meta.primary` to every route |
| `src/router/navigate.js` | device guard: on `phone`, `codx-junior-split` redirects to the last non-desktop route (or `home`) |
| `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` | delete the whole `v-if="isMobile"` branch (the shell owns the drawer) |
| `src/components/ChatEntryMobile.vue` | **create** — D6 is a hard blocker (see §7) |
| `src/components/mobile/MenuBar.vue` | delete (orphaned, unimported children) |

## 5. Defects this closes

| D | Closed? | How |
|---|---|---|
| D1 three breakpoints | ✅ | `useViewport` is the only reader of `innerWidth` |
| D2 no navigation on phone | ✅ | bottom bar is always rendered, independent of route changes |
| D3 no page chrome | ✅ | app bar + one scroll container |
| D4 URL decides mode | ✅ | guard: a phone never mounts `.../desktop` |
| D6 missing chat mobile component | ✅ | created (or the fork deleted — see §7) |
| D7 orphan mobile code | ✅ | `MenuBar.vue` and the `isMobile` sidebar branch removed |
| D9 no primitives | ✅ | shell ships back/title/safe areas/scroll |
| D5 payload hand-off | ❌ | untouched |
| D8 registry bypass | ❌ | untouched (`openMediaLibrary`, `browsers.open`) |
| D10 registry/router divergence | ❌ | untouched |

§7 duplication map is untouched: chat, workspaces, browsers and home still ship two components.

## 6. Effort, risk, rollout

| | |
|---|---|
| Effort | ~1 sprint (1 dev + design review), no screen rewrites |
| Risk | **low** — additive; the desktop path is untouched and the shell is behind a flag |
| Rollout | `feature flag: ui.mobileShell`, default off, on for the team first |
| Reversibility | high — delete one wrapper and the meta fields |
| Known degradation | kanban board, file explorer (256 px tree), vibe coding splitter, infra tables remain cramped; horizontal scroll only |

## 7. The D6 decision (must be taken inside this increment)

`ChatEntry.vue` imports `./ChatEntryMobile.vue`, which does not exist → no mobile message
rendering at all. Two options:

- **A1 (cheap):** create a thin `ChatEntryMobile.vue` that re-uses the desktop template in a
  single column (markdown + collapsible tool calls, no diff panel).
- **A2 (right):** delete the fork and make `ChatEntry.vue` responsive with container queries.

Approach A can ship with A1; approach B requires A2.

## 8. Acceptance criteria

1. On a 390 × 844 device, from cold start: Home → Tasks → a task → back → Chat → back:
   every step reachable in ≤ 2 taps and no screen without a visible back affordance.
2. Opening `/:project/home` on a phone, then pasting `/:project/desktop`, does **not** mount
   dockview (redirects instead).
3. Nothing sits under the iOS home indicator or the status bar (safe-area check on a notched device).
4. `$ui.isMobile` is no longer read outside `useViewport` (grep == 0 hits).
5. Chat renders messages at 390 px (D6 closed) — no console error, no blank bubbles.
6. Desktop: identical layout, identical saved dockview layouts (`projectLayout_<project>` intact).

## 9. Why this might be the right answer

It converts a *blocked* product (no navigation) into a *usable* one in one sprint, keeps the
desktop unaffected, and produces the shell + primitives (`useViewport`, app bar, bottom bar,
guards) that approaches B and C need anyway. Its weakness is honest: it does not fix the
inconsistency between screens — it only stops the inconsistency from being *fatal*.

# Approach B — Adaptive page contract ("one component, two densities")

> Status: proposed · Part of the **Mobile Refactor** board (design decision pending).
> Owner of the design: Mockups / Designer · Reviewer: board owner.
> Fixes the *inconsistency*: one screen definition, rendered at two densities.

---

## 1. Idea

Instead of wrapping the current screens, **change what a screen is**. Every screen declares
its own chrome through a single contract — title, back, actions, scroll behaviour — and the
contract is rendered by the mode, not by the screen. Screens stop building headers, drawers
and scroll containers; the duplicate desktop/mobile component pairs are collapsed into one
adaptive component each.

The user-visible result: the same product at 390 px and at 1600 px, with the *same* features,
laid out differently — not two products that happen to share a colour scheme.

```
PHONE (390)                    TABLET (768)                DESKTOP (unchanged)
┌───────────────┐              ┌───────────────────────┐    ┌────┬──────────────────────┐
│ ‹  Chat    ⋯  │              │ ‹  Chat           ⋯   │    │rail│  dockview panels     │
├───────────────┤              ├──────────┬────────────┤    │    │  (ChatView, Kanban…) │
│ messages      │              │ list     │ messages   │    │    │                      │
│               │  ← same      │ (rail)   │            │    │    │                      │
├───────────────┤    component │          │            │    │    │                      │
│ [ composer ]  │              ├──────────┴────────────┤    │    │                      │
└───────────────┘              │ [ composer ]          │    │    │                      │
                               └───────────────────────┘    └────┴──────────────────────┘
```

## 2. The contract

```vue
<!-- src/components/mobile/MobilePage.vue  (rendered by the shell in mobile mode) -->
<MobilePage :title="title" :back="back" :actions="actions" :pad="false">
  <ChatConversation />          <!-- the screen's real content, nothing else -->
</MobilePage>
```

Rules:

1. A screen **never** renders a top bar, a drawer, or a full-height scroll container.
2. A screen **never** reads `window.innerWidth`; it reads `useViewport()` only to choose a
   *density*, not to fork into another component.
3. A screen declares `meta.title` / `meta.parent` / `meta.actions` in the router, so the shell
   can render chrome before the screen chunk even loads (skeleton ≠ blank).
4. Identity comes from the URL; the screen fetches its object on mount (kills the `PENDING`
   map, D5).
5. Layout differences are expressed with **container queries** on the page root
   (`@container`), not with `v-if` on a global flag — a dockview panel at 500 px wide behaves
   like a phone even on a desktop.

## 3. What changes

**New primitives**

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/components/mobile/MobilePage.vue` | app bar + content slot + scroll owner + safe areas |
| `src/components/mobile/MobileList.vue` / `MobileListItem.vue` | list → detail pattern used by kanban, files, teams, knowledge |
| `src/components/mobile/MoreSheet.vue` | registry grouped in the desktop sidebar's sections |
| `src/composables/useViewport.js` | `phone` / `tablet` / `desktop`, single breakpoint table |

**Screens consolidated (duplicate removed)**

| Kept | Deleted | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `views/ChatView.vue` (adaptive) | `views/QuickChatView.vue`, `components/ChatEntryMobile.vue` | chat becomes **one** component; `ChatEntry` loses the `$ui.isMobile` fork |
| `components/workspaces/WorkspacesManager.vue` (adaptive) | `views/WorkspaceView.vue` | |
| `components/browsers/BrowserSessionList.vue` (adaptive) | `components/browsers/BrowsersSessionManager.vue` | also fixes `browser-viewer` (D8) |
| `views/ManagementDashboardView.vue` | `views/CodxWelcomeView.vue` | one Home |
| `views/GlobalSettings.vue` | the second (mobile) markup branch *inside the same file* | 10 duplicated blocks → 1 |

**Screens that must be re-laid out (not just re-wrapped)**

`KanbanBoardView.vue` (columns → vertically paged columns), `FileExplorerPanel.vue`
(tree → drill-down list), `VibeCodingView.vue` (splitter → tabs), `InfraView.vue`
(tables → cards), `views/TeamView.vue` (`TeamBar` → sheet).

**Shell / plumbing**

`src/App.vue` (shell only), `src/store/ui.js` (drop `isMobile`, keep `viewport`),
`src/router/index.ts` (`meta` on every route + `/desktop` device guard),
`src/config/apps.js` + `src/config/appComponentsMap.js` (one table, asserted equal by a test),
`src/router/navigate.js` (`openApp` is the only opener; delete the `browsers.open` bypass).

## 4. Defects this closes

| D | Closed? | How |
|---|---|---|
| D1 three breakpoints | ✅ | `useViewport` + container queries |
| D2 no navigation | ✅ | shell (bottom bar + More sheet) |
| D3 no page chrome | ✅ | `MobilePage` contract |
| D4 URL decides mode | ✅ | device guard + container queries make width, not URL, the driver |
| D5 in-memory payload | ✅ | identity in the URL, object fetched on mount |
| D6 missing chat component | ✅ | the fork is deleted, not implemented |
| D7 orphan mobile code | ✅ | `MenuBar`, sidebar mobile branch, `SplitView`/`Splitter` |
| D8 registry bypass | ✅ | all openers funnel through `openApp` |
| D9 no primitives | ✅ | `MobilePage` / `MobileList` / `MoreSheet` |
| D10 registry/router divergence | ✅ | single table + test |
| §7 duplication | ✅ | 6 duplicate pairs collapsed |

## 5. Effort, risk, rollout

| | |
|---|---|
| Effort | 2–3 sprints, ~15 screens touched, 4 screens re-laid out |
| Risk | **medium-high** — touches the screens people use daily; needs the D6/D5 decisions taken first |
| Rollout | per-screen increment: each migration is one PR, behind `ui.mobilePages`, merged screen by screen |
| Reversibility | medium — deleting the duplicate component is irreversible per screen, hence the flag |
| Biggest trap | `useViewport` *and* container queries both exist; a screen that uses the global flag will look right in the browser test and wrong inside a narrow dockview panel |

## 6. Sequencing (if chosen)

1. Primitives + shell (same code as approach A §4 — the two approaches share M1).
2. Fix D6 properly (delete `ChatEntryMobile`, make `ChatEntry` adaptive).
3. Migrate Chat (proves list→detail + composer + keyboard).
4. Migrate Tasks (proves the dense board).
5. Migrate the four "cannot adapt" screens.
6. Sweep the remaining `@/views/*` screens to the contract; delete duplicates at the end of each PR.
7. Add the registry/router equality test (C5: the project has almost no tests).

## 7. Acceptance criteria

1. For chat, workspaces, browsers and home there is **exactly one** component; a repo search
   for `QuickChatView`, `WorkspaceView`, `BrowsersSessionManager`, `CodxWelcomeView`,
   `ChatEntryMobile` returns zero hits.
2. No screen contains a top bar, a `drawer`, or `window.innerWidth` (grep == 0 outside `useViewport`).
3. Every screen renders correctly inside a 500 px wide dockview panel on desktop (container
   query proof) **and** at 390 px on a phone.
4. Refresh on a deep link (`/:project/chat/:id/:name`, `/:project/kanban/:board`) renders the
   object from the URL with the `PENDING` map removed.
5. `appKey → route → component` is asserted by an automated test.

## 8. Why this might be the right answer

It is the only approach that removes the *reason* the pages are inconsistent: two UI stacks.
The cost is honest: it is the approach with the most screen churn, the most mockups needed
(two densities per screen), and the one that most needs the test suite the project does not
have yet.

# Approach C — Launcher + stack ("mobile is its own product surface")

> Status: proposed · Part of the **Mobile Refactor** board (design decision pending).
> Owner of the design: Mockups / Designer · Reviewer: board owner.
> Fixes the *model*: phones get a navigation architecture of their own, not a squeezed desktop.

---

## 1. Idea

Approach A wraps the current screens; approach B makes one screen adapt. Approach C accepts
that **a workspace of 35 apps cannot be a phone menu** and gives the phone its own surface:

- a **Launcher** as the landing screen (the modules that make sense on a phone, big targets,
  recents at the top);
- a **per-module stack**: entering a module pushes a stack, "back" pops it, and the bottom
  bar is always reachable (it never changes meaning);
- a small, explicit **mobile registry**: for each `appKey`, an icon, a title, a "fits on a
  phone?" flag, and optionally a dedicated mobile component — so the 12 apps that do *not*
  fit on a phone are not silently cramped, they are routed to a "open on desktop" screen or
  to a list-shaped alternative.

Desktop is untouched. The route tree stays the same (deep links work), but the *phone*
resolves the same URL into a stack-aware surface.

```
LAUNCHER                     STACK (within a module)          BOTTOM BAR (constant)
┌───────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────┐            ┌───────────────────┐
│ codx-junior    ⌄  │        │ ‹  Task Manager ⋯ │            │  ⌂      ✓      💬 │
│ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ │  tap   ├───────────────────┤   always   │ Home  Tasks  Chat │
│ │ ✓ │ │ 💬│ │ 📁│ │ ─────► │ Backlog   (3)     │   visible  ├───────────────────┤
│ └───┘ └───┘ └───┘ │        │  · task card      │            │   📁      ⊞       │
│ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ ┌───┐ │        │  · task card      │            │ Files   More      │
│ │ 👥│ │ ⚙ │ │ ⋯ │ │        ├───────────────────┤            └───────────────────┘
│ └───┘ └───┘ └───┘ │        │ [ + New task    ] │
│ Recents           │        └───────────────────┘
└───────────────────┘
```

## 2. Navigation model

**Three levels, never more**

| Level | Surface | Example |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | Launcher (`/:project/home` on phone) | module grid + recents + project switcher |
| L1 | Module root | Task Manager boards list, Files roots, Chat list |
| L2 | Detail | a task, a file, a conversation |

The bottom bar is a **sibling of the stack**, not part of it: tapping a bar item *resets* to
that module's L1 (second tap on the active item pops to L1, third does nothing).

**Back rules (explicit, not browser history)**

| Situation | Back does |
|---|---|
| L2 in a module | pop to that module's L1 |
| L1 | pop to the Launcher |
| Launcher | nothing (no dead history exit) |
| Deep link into L2 | synthesize the stack: L1 + L2, so back lands on a real screen |

**"More" sheet** holds the full registry (same sections as the desktop sidebar:
Apps / Workspaces / Account), with a `phone-friendly` badge per app and an
"open on desktop" action for the ones that are not.

## 3. The mobile registry (the core of this approach)

```js
// src/config/mobileApps.js  — the ONLY place that decides "can a phone do this?"
export const MOBILE_APPS = {
  tasks:   { order: 10, primary: true,  title: 'Tasks',  icon: 'fa-list-check',
             entry: 'kanban', fits: 'list',  mobileComponent: null },

"forgotten" on mobile again — which is exactly the failure mode today.

## 4. What changes

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/config/mobileApps.js` | **new** — the registry above |
| `src/composables/useMobileStack.js` | **new** — stack push/pop, resets per bar item, deep-link synthesis |
| `src/components/mobile/MobileLauncher.vue` | **new** — L0 grid + recents |
| `src/components/mobile/MobileBar.vue` | extends `MobileBottomBar.vue`; items come from the registry, not hardcoded |
| `src/components/mobile/MoreSheet.vue` | **new** — full registry + badges + "open on desktop" |
| `src/components/mobile/StackHeader.vue` | **new** — ‹ + title + ⋯ built from the stack, not from `meta` |
| `src/components/mobile/mobileViews/MobileKanban.vue`, `MobileFileList.vue`, `OpenOnDesktopNotice.vue` | **new** — the 3–4 screens that genuinely need a phone layout |
| `src/router/index.ts` | `/:project/home` resolves to `MobileLauncher` **only** on phone (single resolution point, not `meta.app`) |
| `src/router/navigate.js` | `openApp` chooses the surface: desktop panel / stack push / `desktop-only` notice |
| `src/App.vue`, `src/store/ui.js`, `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` | shell + `useViewport` + delete the mobile drawer branch (same as A) |
| `src/components/ChatEntryMobile.vue` | **create** (D6 blocker) — or delete the fork as in B |

## 5. Defects this closes

| D | Closed? | How |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | ✅ | `useViewport` |
| D2 | ✅ | bar + launcher, both always visible |
| D3 | ✅ | `StackHeader` owns the chrome |
| D4 | ✅ | device decides the surface; `.../desktop` on a phone → launcher |
| D6 | ✅ | created/deleted before the first demo |
| D7 | ✅ | drawer mobile branch + `MenuBar` + `SplitView`/`Splitter` |
| D8 | ✅ | `openApp` is the only opener and it now also decides the surface |
| D9 | ✅ | shell + bar + header + sheet |
| D10 | ✅ | `MOBILE_APPS` keyed by `APPS` key, asserted by test |
| D5 | ⚠️ partial | the L2 stack needs identity in the URL anyway → effectively closed for the modules on the bar; the rest keeps `PENDING` until migrated |
| §7 duplication | ⚠️ partial | chat/files get one mobile component; global settings stays duplicated until migrated |

## 6. Effort, risk, rollout

| | |
|---|---|
| Effort | 3–4 sprints; 1 registry + 5 new components + 3–4 mobile-specific screens |
| Risk | **high** — it changes how the phone resolves routes, which is the highest-blast-radius change in the list |
| Rollout | `feature flag: ui.mobileLauncher` + `MOBILE_APPS.fits` can be rolled out per app (an app marked `desktop-only` simply shows the notice) |
| Reversibility | medium — the registry is additive, the launcher landing is a single route resolution |
| Design cost | highest — every bar item, the launcher grid, the sheet and the stack header need mockups |

## 7. Acceptance criteria

1. From the Launcher, any phone-friendly app is reachable in ≤ 2 taps; any desktop-only app is
   *labelled* as such instead of rendering a broken layout.
2. Back never exits the app: L2 → L1 → Launcher → (no-op).
3. Opening a deep link `/:project/kanban/:board` on a phone synthesizes L1 + L2 and back lands
   on the boards list.
4. Every key of `APPS` has exactly one `MOBILE_APPS` entry (automated test).
5. After 5 minutes of use the bar has not changed meaning (same 4 destinations, same order).
6. Desktop: byte-identical dockview behaviour, saved layouts unaffected.

## 8. Why this might be the right answer

It is the only approach that answers the two questions the other two dodge: *"35 apps do not
fit in 5 slots"* and *"some screens cannot be squeezed"*. It gives each screen an explicit,
reviewable mobile status (`fits`) instead of an implicit one (nobody ever tried). It is also
the most expensive and the only one that changes the mental model of the product, so it needs
product sign-off, not only engineering sign-off.

## 9. Why it might be too much

If the mobile audience is "check my tasks and answer a chat while away", then a launcher grid
plus a stack is more architecture than the usage justifies — approach A gets 80 % of the
value in 20 % of the time. The decision hinges on whether mobile is a **support surface** or a
**first-class surface**.

| # | Document | What it is | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

| 5 | [`approaches/02-adaptive-pages.md`](./approaches/02-adaptive-pages.md) | **Approach B** — one component per screen with two densities; removes the duplication | proposed |
| 6 | [`approaches/03-launcher-stack.md`](./approaches/03-launcher-stack.md) | **Approach C** — launcher + per-module stack + mobile registry; phone as its own surface | proposed |

## 2. The three approaches at a glance

| | A · Shell-first | B · Adaptive pages | C · Launcher + stack |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nav surface | bottom bar (5) + More sheet | bottom bar + More sheet + per-screen patterns | launcher (L0) + constant bottom bar (4) + More sheet |
| Back | `router.back()` / `meta.parent` | `meta.parent` + container-query layouts | explicit stack (L2→L1→Launcher) |
| Screens rewritten | 0 | ~15 migrated, 4 re-laid out | 3–4 new mobile-specific screens + launcher/sheet |
| Fixes | D1, D2, D3, D4, D6, D7, D9 | **all of D1–D10 + §7 duplication** | D1–D4, D6–D10 (D5 partial) |
| Leaves broken | D5, D8, D10, all duplication | — | `PENDING` map for non-migrated modules |
| Effort | ~1 sprint | 2–3 sprints | 3–4 sprints |
| Risk | low | medium-high | high |
| Reversible | yes (one wrapper) | per screen (flag) | yes (registry + one route) |
| Design cost | 1 shell + 5 bar items | shell + 2 densities × ~15 screens | launcher + stack + sheet + 4 mobile screens |

**Shared foundation (identical in all three):** `useViewport()` as the single breakpoint
source, one shell that owns scroll + safe areas, a `/desktop` device guard, a mounted
navigation surface, and the D6 chat fix. Whichever approach is chosen, the first increment is
the same.

## 3. Recommendation (for the decision record — not a decision)

Ship **A first, behind `ui.mobileShell`**, because the product currently has *no* usable
phone navigation and A is the only approach that can close D2/D3/D6 without touching a screen.
Then treat **B as the migration path** per screen (it is A's shell plus a per-screen contract,
so no work is thrown away) and adopt **C's `MOBILE_APPS.fits` registry idea** even if the
launcher itself is not built — a per-app "does this fit on a phone?" flag is what prevents the
current failure mode from coming back.

C is the right answer only if mobile is decided to be a first-class surface.

## 4. Decision record (fill when the approaches are reviewed)

```md

Decided by:
Date:
Rationale:
Rejected because:
First increment (M1) scope:

1. Is mobile a **support surface** (triage chat + tasks) or a **first-class surface**?
2. `ChatEntryMobile.vue`: create the thin component (A/C) or delete the fork and make
   `ChatEntry` responsive (B)?
3. Do chat / workspaces / browsers keep two components, or is collapsing them in scope?
